title: Your First Map
story: Your teacher posted exam scores on the bulletin board: Alice got 95, Bob got 87, Charlie got 92. To find Bob's score, you scan the whole list. But what if there were 500 students? You need a way to jump straight to any name and see their score instantly.
why: Map[K,V] pairs keys with values for O(1) lookups — unlike Vec where you must scan every element to find a match.
analogy: A Map is like a phone book. You look up a name (key) to find a phone number (value). You don't scan every page — you jump directly to the name. Unlike a Vec which is like a numbered list where you need to know the exact position.
try_it: Create a Map[Str,Int] of country populations. Add 5 countries. Look up one that exists and one that doesn't. What happens if you insert the same key twice with different values? Try creating a Map[Int,Str] where keys are ID numbers and values are names — reverse the key-value pattern.
tips: Map keys must be unique — inserting the same key again replaces the old value
`.get()` always returns `Option[V]` — you must handle the case where the key doesn't exist
Choose meaningful keys: `Map[Str,Int]` for name-to-score is better than `Map[Int,Int]` where you'd need to memorize ID numbers
common_mistakes: Expecting `.get()` to return the value directly — it returns `Option[V]`, so you must unwrap with match
Using the wrong key type: `phonebook.get(42)` when the map is `Map[Str,Str]` — keys must match the declared type
Thinking Map preserves insertion order — like most hash maps, order is NOT guaranteed
